Petitioners
 Through: Ms. Mamta Chandra, Adv with
 petitioners in person
 versus
 State (Gnct Of Delhi) & Anr. .....
Respondents  Through: Mr. Pradeep Gahlot, APP for the State  SI Seema, PS Najafgarh  R-2 in person

CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ANISH DAYAL  ORDER % 18.04.2023 CRL.M.A. 10149/2023 1.
Exemption allowed subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

1. This petition has been filed seeking quashing of FIR No.175/2014 under sections 498A/406/323/506/34 IPC PS Najafgarh on the ground that the parties have arrived at a settlement vide settlement dated 4th December, 2021, arrived at with the facilitation of Mediation Centre, Dwarka Courts, which is on record of this Court.
2. Petitioner nos. 1 and 2 and respondent no.2-complainant are present in the Court and have been duly identified by the Investigating Officer and their counsel.
3. Petitioner No. 1 and respondent No. 2 were married on 15th February, 2013 and one male child was born out of wedlock.
Pursuant to the differences between themselves they have now obtained decree of divorce by mutual consent dated 25th February, 2023.

4. As per the settlement, a sum of Rs.5,50,000/- is to be paid to respondent no. 2 by the petitioner no.1 at this stage which is tendered by way of Demand Draft No. 976232 dated 4th February, 2023 drawn on Bank which she has received and acknowledged in the Court.
She further submits that she has no objection to quashing of the FIR.

5. Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the Naveen Kumar & Anr vs State (Gnct Of Delhi) & Anr on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112435616/
1

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: petitioners being remote and bleak, there is no use continuing with proceedings of the present FIR as it would be a misuse of the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, the FIR No.175/2014 under sections 498A/406/323/506/34 IPC PS Najafgarh oand proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
It is however made clear that the said settlement will not affect the rights of the minor child in future.
6. Parties shall abide by the terms of settlement.

7. Petition stands disposed of accordingly.
8. Pending applications (if any) are disposed of as infructuous.
9. Order be uploaded on the website of this Court.
